name: Tangalle
line: Long, quiet beaches at the far end of the south coast.

image.alt: A couple walking a palm-lined beach at sunset

summary: Long, empty beaches at the far end of the south coast, and the easiest place on the island to do nothing for a few days.

intro.heading: The quiet end of the coast.
paragraphs: East of Mirissa the south coast empties out. Tangalle is a small market town with long beaches either side of it, many of them backed by nothing but palms and a handful of villas.
This is where we end a lot of journeys. After the hills and the parks, three nights here with nowhere to be is often what people remember most fondly. Yala is close enough for a day, if you want one.

mapCaption: Towards the eastern end of the south coast. The other dots are the places we pair it with.

doing.lede: Tangalle is a place to slow down. These are the things we build the days around, when there is anything at all.

items.title: A different beach each day
items.body: Goyambokka, Silent Beach, Rekawa and Marakolliya are all a short tuk-tuk ride apart, and none of them is ever busy.

items.title: Turtles at Rekawa
items.body: Green turtles come ashore to nest on most nights of the year. A local conservation project watches the beach and calls you when one arrives.

items.title: The rock temple at Mulkirigala
items.body: Cave shrines stacked up a rock inland, quieter than Dambulla and a good morning’s climb.

items.title: Long lunches
items.body: Grilled fish, a cold drink and a hammock. We choose stays that are good at all three.

gallery.alt: A lone walker on a wide, empty beach
Palms, sand and reef from above

season: Tangalle follows the south coast: at its best from December to April, and wet from May to September. The sea is rough in the monsoon months, so swimming is for the dry season.
ctaBody: Tell us your dates and we will fit it in, with a few days at the end with nothing planned.
